title: Causal Role of Instruction-Following Training in Emergent Misalignment Susceptibility
original_idea: Compare emergent misalignment induction on models with weak vs. strong instruction-following training (same base, different IF fine-tuning intensity). Measure whether IF training level predicts emergent misalignment susceptibility.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: stronger IF training -> broader compliance generalization -> higher emergent misalignment susceptibility. The safety implication (fundamental tension between compliance and alignment) is clearly articulated and critical for training design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires access to or creation of models with varying IF training intensity from the same base, plus inducing emergent misalignment. Obtaining or creating controlled IF-intensity variants is advanced. Misalignment induction adds further complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires preparing multiple model variants with controlled IF intensity and then inducing/measuring misalignment on each. A first deliverable (two variants) is possible but the setup effort for controlled IF intensity variants is substantial within 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: No novelty assessment available; default estimated score assigned.
